title: What If You Cried in Space? Tears Don't Fall

scenes.text: What if you cried in space? Your eyes still make tears. They just never fall.
On Earth, gravity pulls tears down your cheeks. In orbit, there's nothing to pull them anywhere.
Instead, the tears stay put and form a ball of water that clings to your eye.
Keep crying and the ball keeps growing. Astronaut Chris Hadfield said you just end up with a bigger and bigger ball of water.
Eventually it can spread across your nose to the other eye, and loose drops can float off into the cabin.
Hadfield's fix was a towel. In space, even crying turns into a cleanup job.

description:
What if you cried in space?
Without gravity, tears don't fall. They form a growing ball of water on your eye, as astronaut Chris Hadfield showed.
